definitions.meaning: Billingsgate is London's famous fish market, so its display would be a stall laid out with fish, read as three words
reserved here means aloof, cool and distant in manner

explanation.surface: A fishmonger's showy patter at the market turns out to be quite shy.
explanation.walkthrough: Billingsgate is the old London fish market, notorious for its traders' foul language; split the answer as STAND OF FISH and it describes a market stall.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: a market stall of fish, and an aloof, unfriendly manner.

parts.note: the famous First World War fighter biplane named Camel, rather than an airborne animal

explanation.walkthrough: The Camel was a British WWI fighter aircraft built by the Sopwith company.
explanation.definitionFit: The aircraft manufacturer made the Camel, the best-known British fighter plane of 1914-18.

clue.text: Lear's crazed in Cordelia's husband's dominion

indicators.note: Lear goes mad in the play, so his name is scrambled, made crazy

explanation.surface: King Lear goes mad in the realm ruled by his daughter's husband.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crazed' rearranges LEARS. Cordelia marries the King of France, and Arles was once a kingdom within Burgundy, in what is now France.
explanation.definitionFit: The city in southern France was the seat of a medieval kingdom, standing for the French king's realm.

parts.note: the Florida beach town famous for motor racing, so where speedy drivers go

explanation.walkthrough: 'Fast set' suggests a racy social crowd, but it means racing drivers: the beach town hosts the Daytona speedway races.
explanation.definitionFit: The Florida beach town is home to a famous motor-racing speedway and land speed records.

clue.text: Such frivolities are far from bearskins

definitions.text: Such frivolities are far from bearskins

parts.words: Such frivolities are far from bearskins
parts.note: flouncy trimmings on a skirt, which split as fur placed low, the opposite of a guardsman's tall fur hat

explanation.walkthrough: Furbelows are showy flounces; split as FUR BELOW, the opposite of a bearskin, the tall fur cap of British Guards worn on top.
explanation.definitionFit: Showy pleated trimmings on a dress, read as fur at the bottom rather than on the head.

parts.note: the letters IDES complete the nickname of Cromwell's cavalry, so the clue wants the word that goes before them

explanation.walkthrough: Ides suggests the Roman date, but put IRONS before IDES and you get Ironsides, Cromwell's troopers in the English Civil War.
explanation.definitionFit: Joined to the clue's Ides it forms the name of Cromwell's cavalry in the English Civil War.

parts.note: paying attention to something, as to a warning

explanation.definitionFit: Paying attention to advice or a warning means minding it.

parts.note: points both to Swift's satire A Tale of a ... and to the vessel we sit soaking in at bath time

explanation.walkthrough: Jonathan Swift wrote A Tale of a Tub (1704); a tub is also the bath we lie immersed in.
explanation.definitionFit: A bath vessel holds us immersed, and it names the title of Swift's satirical Tale.

clue.text: Not quite in the also-ran class, then?

definitions.text: Not quite in the also-ran class, then?

parts.words: Not quite in the also-ran class, then
parts.note: in a race, finishing just outside the top two but ahead of the unplaced runners

explanation.walkthrough: Literally the horse came third, just above the also-rans; the phrase usually means inferior.
explanation.definitionFit: Of poor quality, and literally the class for coming in behind first and second.

indicators.note: the tree name is wrung out of shape, its letters rearranged

parts.note: beeches are a kind of tree

explanation.surface: A worshipper offers prayers beneath gnarled old trees.
explanation.walkthrough: 'twisted' rearranges BEECHES; the fodder is not printed, only the trees.
explanation.definitionFit: To pray to someone is to implore or entreat them earnestly.

parts.note: a heroine created by John Gay, read as if it meant a cheerful young woman

explanation.walkthrough: Gay is the playwright John Gay: Polly Peachum is the heroine of The Beggar's Opera, and its sequel bears her name.
explanation.definitionFit: Peachum's daughter in The Beggar's Opera is the leading girl of the dramatist Gay.

indicators.note: the chess pieces are placed round the lake, enclosing it

parts.note: in chess the castle is also called the rook
Erie is one of the North American Great Lakes

explanation.surface: A ruined pair of castles sits on either side of some lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Slum' is used in its old sense: a rookery was a crowded tenement district, named for the noisy, packed nesting colonies of rooks.
explanation.definitionFit: A rookery was a densely packed, squalid tenement district, the old sense of a slum.

clue.text: Coming to us, having already arrived at the supermarket

definitions.meaning: something coming our way in the future is waiting for us, as in a surprise held for us

definitions.text: having already arrived at the supermarket
definitions.meaning: goods already sitting in the shop rather than on order, as in a supermarket's own bakery

explanation.surface: A delivery heading our way has already turned up at the shop.
explanation.definitionFit: One phrase means both lying ahead for someone and located within a shop.

parts.note: the verb in its slang sense of cheating someone, as in being done out of money

explanation.definitionFit: To do someone is slang for cheating them out of money by fraud.

definitions.meaning: the Jutes were a Germanic people who came to Britain; one of their legendary leaders arrived with his brother Hengist
the Airspeed troop-carrying glider of the Second World War bore this leader's name

explanation.surface: Bales of jute fibre are brought in by air on a glider.
explanation.walkthrough: Jute looks like the fibre, but it means a member of the Jutish people: Hengist and Horsa led the Jutes into Kent. The British Airspeed Horsa was a WWII glider.
explanation.definitionFit: A Jutish chieftain who settled in Kent, and the wartime British transport glider named after him.

parts.note: plays on blue blood, the phrase for aristocratic birth, applied to monarchs

explanation.walkthrough: Blue blood means noble descent, so a king's blood would be the regal shade of blue.
explanation.definitionFit: Aristocrats are said to have blue blood, so monarchs' blood would be the deep regal shade.

clue.text: Picture that plots a petroleum company's progress?

definitions.meaning: a kind of print imitating an oil painting

definitions.text: that plots a petroleum company's progress?
definitions.meaning: split as oil plus chart: a chart that plots how an oil firm is doing

explanation.surface: An oil firm commissions a chart to track its fortunes.
explanation.walkthrough: An oleograph is a print made to look like an oil painting; the second reading splits it as OLEO (oil) plus GRAPH, a chart of progress.
explanation.definitionFit: A lithographic print in imitation of oil paint, and, read literally, an oil chart.

clue.text: Neat moon shot signalized this occurrence between China and Argentine ware

definitions.text: Neat moon shot signalized this occurrence between China and Argentine ware

parts.words: Neat moon shot signalized this occurrence between China and Argentine ware
parts.note: the nursery rhyme in which the cow jumps over the moon and the dish runs away with the spoon

explanation.walkthrough: Neat means cattle: in Hey Diddle Diddle the cow jumps over the moon, and the dish (china) runs away with the spoon (silver, Argentine ware).
explanation.definitionFit: The dish running off with the spoon is a runaway romance of the kind lovers make to Gretna.

clue.text: "Quick, while the sun shines, I conjure ye !" as a farmer might be heard to cry

indicators.note: what the farmer calls out is taken by its sound, matching a familiar magician's cry

parts.note: make hay while the sun shines, done presto, that is quickly: a farmer's call to get the hay in fast

explanation.surface: A farmer urges his hands to hurry with the haymaking before the weather breaks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'might be heard' signals the sound-alike: HAY PRESTO, the farmer's cry to bring in the hay fast while the sun shines, is said like the conjuror's exclamation.
explanation.definitionFit: The stage magician's exclamation at the moment a trick is revealed.

parts.note: Byron wrote a collection of poems called Hebrew Melodies

explanation.walkthrough: Byron's Hebrew Melodies (1815) includes She Walks in Beauty.
explanation.definitionFit: Byron's poem collection was titled Hebrew Melodies, so they are Jewish in character.

clue.text: Cleric, not yet canonized in Hunts, resurrects

parts.note: Rev is short for Reverend, a cleric's title
St Ives is a town in Huntingdonshire; before its saint is made a saint, it is just Ives

explanation.surface: A vicar from Huntingdonshire who has not yet been made a saint brings people back to life.
explanation.walkthrough: Huntingdonshire (Hunts) is a former English county containing St Ives; take away the St, as if the saint were not yet canonized.
explanation.definitionFit: To revive something is to bring it back to life or into use again.

clue.text: She was told to thank heaven fasting for a good man's love

definitions.text: She was told to thank heaven fasting for a good man's love

parts.words: She was told to thank heaven fasting for a good man's love
parts.note: a quotation from Shakespeare: Rosalind scolds the proud shepherdess who scorns Silvius

explanation.walkthrough: In As You Like It, Rosalind tells the shepherdess Phebe: 'down on your knees, And thank heaven, fasting, for a good man's love.'
explanation.definitionFit: The scornful shepherdess in As You Like It is the woman Rosalind lectures with those words.

clue.text: Somewhere in the Mediterranean for one of our lighter moments

parts.note: paler means lighter in colour
mo is short for a moment, as in half a mo

explanation.surface: A Mediterranean holiday is remembered as one of our happier, more carefree times.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lighter moments' suggests fun, but lighter means PALER and a moment is a MO.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sicilian capital city lies on the Mediterranean coast.

parts.note: Mrs Gaskell's ladies of Cranford practise a genteel thrift she gives a famous two-word name

explanation.walkthrough: In Elizabeth Gaskell's novel Cranford the ladies' genteel penny-pinching is called 'elegant economy'.
explanation.definitionFit: Gaskell's phrase for the refined thrift of Cranford's ladies pairs economy with this graceful word.

parts.note: the Venezuelan general known as El Libertador, who freed much of South America from Spain

explanation.definitionFit: Simón, the South American revolutionary leader, was called El Libertador.

parts.note: a baron of beef is a large joint, and to rule this is an old form of rule the roost

explanation.walkthrough: A baron of beef is a double sirloin joint; 'rule the roast' is the old form of the idiom 'rule the roost'.
explanation.definitionFit: A baron of beef is a cooked joint, and one rules this in the old idiom for being in charge.

clue.text: In which Lycidas's ship was built

definitions.text: In which Lycidas's ship was built

parts.words: In which Lycidas's ship was built
parts.note: Milton's elegy blames the fatal bark, built under an ill-omened darkening of the sun

explanation.walkthrough: Milton's Lycidas: 'It was that fatal and perfidious bark, Built in th' eclipse, and rigged with curses dark.' The clue reads as if naming a shipyard.
explanation.definitionFit: In Milton's poem the ill-fated vessel was built during an ominous darkening of the sun.

clue.text: This could be' the point of making hay

definitions.text: This could be' the point of making hay

parts.words: This could be' the point of making hay
parts.note: the tine of a pitchfork used to toss hay, rather than the purpose of haymaking

explanation.walkthrough: 'The point' sounds like the purpose, but it is a literal point: a tine of the hayfork.
explanation.definitionFit: One spike of a pitchfork is the sharp tip used in haymaking.

clue.text: Relieve a tribe in a late encompassment

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the tribe is placed in the words that follow, sitting inside them
the outer letters encompass, that is surround, the tribe

parts.note: taken as written
Levi is one of the twelve tribes of Israel

explanation.surface: Bringing a tribe help when it is besieged too late.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a tribe' tempts you to take the article with the tribe; it is the second 'a' that supplies a letter, opening the late word.
explanation.definitionFit: To alleviate pain or hardship is to ease or lessen it.

parts.note: a novel by George Meredith whose heroine's surname is Fleming, so a Fleming put into a book

explanation.walkthrough: Rhoda Fleming (1865) is a novel by George Meredith; 'brought to book' usually means punished, but here a Fleming is put into a book.
explanation.definitionFit: Meredith's novel takes its title from this heroine with the surname Fleming.

definitions.meaning: the word or action telling an actor to begin speaking
in billiards a cannon is a shot, and it is started with the player's stick

explanation.surface: Someone gives the order for the artillery to begin firing.
explanation.walkthrough: A cannon looks like artillery, but in billiards it is a shot hitting two balls in turn, played with a cue.
explanation.definitionFit: Both an actor's prompt to begin and the billiards stick that strikes for a cannon shot.

clue.text: Put dial right back and disregard it

definitions.meaning: turn a dial or meter right round to its zero mark
an old idiom meaning to treat something as worthless and ignore it

explanation.surface: Reset the meter to zero and pay no attention to it.
explanation.definitionFit: To reset a gauge to zero, and an idiom for treating something with contempt.
